title: Delivery Claims Repeat-Claim Limit (Claims Review Board Ruling)
content:
**Ruling.** Delivery Claims are read across all of the customer's orders. Where the claim type's repeat limit is above zero, a claim of that type is denied with the reason repeat claim limit when the customer already has that many claims of the same type approved or resolved in the trailing 12 months, unless a police report reference is logged on the claim, in which case it is decided normally. The limit counts approvals only; denied and withdrawn claims never count.

## What is counted

- The customer's claims of the same claim type, on any of their orders.
- Only claims whose status is approved or resolved.
- Only those decided in the trailing 12 calendar months ending today, by their decision date.
- Denied claims and withdrawn claims are never counted.

## Decision table

| Repeat limit for the type | Same-type approved or resolved claims in the trailing 12 months | Police report reference on this claim | Outcome on this point |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | any number | — | no limit applies |
| above 0 | fewer than the limit | — | the limit does not stop the claim |
| above 0 | equal to or more than the limit | not logged | denied, reason repeat claim limit |
| above 0 | equal to or more than the limit | logged | decided normally |

## Worked cases (hypothetical, for a type with a limit of 2)

- Two same-type claims resolved in the last 12 months, no police report on the new claim: the customer already has 2, the limit is reached, and the new claim is denied for the repeat claim limit.
- One same-type claim approved and one denied in the last 12 months: only the approved one counts, so the count is 1 and the limit does not stop the claim.
- Two same-type claims approved, one of them decided 13 months ago: only 1 falls in the trailing 12 months, so the limit is not reached.
- Two same-type claims resolved in the last 12 months and a police report reference logged on the new claim: the claim is decided normally.
